# @liha-labs/holiday Full Documentation

`@liha-labs/holiday` is a TypeScript library for Japanese holidays based on official data.

## Principles

- No holiday calculation logic (official data is the source of truth)
- Runtime dependency: zero
- Date string input is strict (`YYYY-MM-DD` only, plus `YYYY-MM` for `listMonth`)
- `Date` input is normalized by local date parts

## Core Types

```ts
type Holiday = { date: 'YYYY-MM-DD'; name: string }
type Weekday = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6
type HolidayDetail = Holiday & { weekday: Weekday }
```

## APIs

```ts
holidayName(input: Date | string): Promise<string | null>
isHoliday(input: Date | string): Promise<boolean>
getHoliday(input: Date | string): Promise<HolidayDetail | null>

listYear(year: number): Promise<HolidayDetail[]>
listMonth(ym: `${number}-${string}`): Promise<HolidayDetail[]>
listRange(start: Date | string, end: Date | string): Promise<HolidayDetail[]>
listAll(): Promise<HolidayDetail[]>

createClient(options?: ClientOptions): HolidayClient
info(): Info
```

## Entries

- `@liha-labs/holiday`: default entry (bundled years + remote year-json for out-of-window years)
- `@liha-labs/holiday/full`: full entry (local-only)

## ClientOptions

```ts
type ClientOptions = {
  remoteBaseUrl?: string
  fetch?: typeof globalThis.fetch
  cache?: 'memory' | 'none'
}
```

## Behavior Notes

- `weekday` is computed at runtime by `new Date(y, m - 1, d).getDay()`
- invalid date strings throw errors (no silent parsing)
- `listRange` is end-inclusive

## Example

```ts
import { createClient, getHoliday } from '@liha-labs/holiday'

const client = createClient({ cache: 'memory' })
const detail = await getHoliday('2026-01-01')
const yearData = await client.listYear(2023)
```
